scope: Bounded independent read-only driver review; no compile, certificate execution, or fault injection.
findings: All package control files, module sources and declared include_str payloads are hash-pinned; canonical module paths and resolved containment reject paths escaping the package.
Literal import declarations are compared to the manifest after nested-comment removal; dependency closure scheduling rejects cycles and requires project imports from the new run output only.

Lean4.32.1 and pinned Mathlib revision are required; lake-manifest dependency revisions and tracked clean state are checked. Direct imported artifacts, including private/server/IR companions, are hashed before and after each compilation.

Each invocation creates a fresh UUID output namespace. Inherited project LEAN_PATH is replaced by this output plus pinned dependency caches and Lean standard library; no prior project output fallback is supplied.

One Lean process uses -j1; the per-build controller admits at most requested jobs with range1..8. A failed compiler stops new admissions, preserves its log/receipt, drains active work, and causes nonzero final status.

The driver launches Lean and read-only toolchain/Git inspection only, with no SAT solver command. Compile-time #eval is rejected; --no-certificate-replay rejects selected LRAT command modules before starting compilers.
Source/data/import/compiler identities are rechecked after compilation; final source/configuration/manifest checks precede PASS.
boundaries: Pinned dependency source and recorded cached artifact hashes constitute the external Lean/Mathlib library boundary; the driver does not independently rebuild those libraries.
Without --no-certificate-replay, selected declared classification proof commands may run in Lean. This is explicit source compilation, not hidden native SAT solving.
Concurrency bound is per invocation; independent simultaneous builds require external host scheduling.
